tasks.task: Forecast units for each product by week or month

items.when: When you have sales history and need a unit forecast per product with a method for each group
When you want a second forecast with the best-fit method named, to compare with your own
When you want a forecast with ranges tested on held-back months, with no model to train
Before the forecast is used for buying, to log each assumption and what would change the answer
When one forecast number is shown with no range and no word on what is unknown

tasks.task: Clean sales history and rebuild demand hidden by stockouts

items.when: Before any forecast, when some products ran out during the sales history
When the export has gaps, duplicates, wrong types and odd spikes to fix first
When the data is cleaned, to report what is still missing or odd and the rules to catch it
When stock sits in Shopify, to find negative or impossible levels that spoil the history

tasks.task: Estimate demand for a new product from similar ones

items.when: When a new product has no history and must borrow a launch curve from similar ones
When you need a low, base and high estimate with every assumption listed
When the first order cannot be topped up, to pick the amount and see the risk of each choice

tasks.task: Check forecast accuracy by product

items.when: After a season or before trusting a forecast for buying, to see which products forecast badly
When you want to test a method on months it has not seen
When a product group needs a different method and a way to track how far off it runs

tasks.task: Set safety stock, reorder points and order quantities

items.when: When you have forecast use, measured lead times and a service level the client chose
When weighing min-max against a fixed order cycle for each product group
When order and holding costs are known, to find the lowest-cost size with discounts compared
When you want a second set of reorder points and an ABC ranking to compare with yours
When the reorder sheet is built, to find formula errors before anyone orders from it

tasks.task: Run the weekly stock and reorder check

items.when: Every week on the same day, before the main supplier's order cut-off
When the check should run itself each week and say whether cash covers the order
When the store is connected and you want days of stock left and draft orders
Before the run, to catch a stock export with blanks or duplicated rows

tasks.task: Plan the cash for the next stock order

items.when: When you have supplier invoices and lead times and need true unit cost and cash needed
When you need order timing, the cash required and a downside case
When cash is tight, to see what better terms would free and what to ask for
When the owner wants to grow, to see whether stock cash or demand is the real limit
Before the cash plan, to take the order quantities it must pay for

tasks.task: Find the cash tied up in slow stock

items.when: When cash is tight, the warehouse is full or a season has ended
When you need stock sorted by how long it has sat unsold
When stock is in Shopify, to list items with units on the shelf and no sales in 90 days
When deciding how to clear it, to plan when and how deep to cut prices

tasks.task: Plan a seasonal buy or a stock build for the busy season

items.when: When a product sells in one season and is ordered once, months ahead
When you have last season's sales, to split the buy into early, held back and markdown
When the budget is fixed, to compare a cautious and a bold buy plan with money and dates
When the stock is made in-house, to plan week by week what to build ahead of the peak
Before committing, to test a downside case and the cash buffer it needs
When the plan only works if the season matches the forecast exactly

tasks.task: Raise purchase orders and follow each to receipt

items.when: When an approved buy list must become orders with price, terms and requested dates
When orders are placed, to get a shared tracker and a notice for the warehouse
When goods cross a border, to list tariff codes, duty options and the papers customs asks for
When a shipment is late, lost or damaged, to get next steps and a carrier claim checklist
When goods arrive, to match order, receipt and invoice line by line

tasks.task: Measure real supplier lead times and reliability

items.when: Before setting safety stock or when deliveries feel late, to replace quoted times with measured
When you need a risk score for each supplier and warning signs to watch
When suppliers miss dates they agreed, to track broken promises and terms to push for

tasks.task: Compare quotes and split an order across suppliers

items.when: Before comparing, to ask every supplier for a quote in the same maker terms
When quotes use different units, currency or delivery terms
When you need minimum order, lead time and deposit risk side by side
When the order should be sized from sales and split to keep cost and risk down
When the split is agreed and each supplier needs its own order pack

tasks.task: Work out landed cost per unit

items.when: When freight, duty and supplier invoices must be spread to a true cost per unit
Before ordering, to see cost per sellable unit and whether the margin still holds
When the sum mixes cartons, units, kilos and currencies, to check each conversion

tasks.task: Cost a product from its bill of materials

items.when: When a product must be costed from parts, scrap allowance, labour and overhead share
When you want a cost sheet by part with the maker and price-break questions for each
When the cost looks high, to break the price into raw parts and find the biggest gaps
When the costed sheet should lead to asks on price and terms
When the cost sheet is built, to find formula errors before prices are set from it

tasks.task: Build a production schedule from open orders

items.when: When open orders must be loaded against each workstation's capacity
When you have a forecast and capacity and need a week-by-week make plan
When jobs compete for machines, to try a job order that meets the due dates
Before a date is promised to a customer, to see the options and the risk of each

tasks.task: Check capacity and find the bottleneck

items.when: When demand may be more than you can make, to find the gaps and a plan to close them
When you have step times, to find the slowest step and rank fixes by output gained
When scrap is high, to get cost per good unit and whether the mix fits the bottleneck
When the mix changes, to recheck profit per good unit against bottleneck hours
When the plan adds capacity before anyone has watched where the work really waits

tasks.task: Turn the schedule into a materials buy list

items.when: When the schedule is set and each part must be bought in time, less what is in stock
When parts are short, to allocate what is available by a priority rule and show what is unfilled
When the buy list is approved and must become orders

tasks.task: Write a quality check plan for a product

items.when: Before the plan, to see each production step where a check could sit
When you have defect data, to rank the biggest causes and plan how to cut them
When goods are made elsewhere, to brief an inspector with a pass rule
When a supplier replies to a defect, to test the reply against your inspection evidence

tasks.task: Run the monthly demand and supply review

items.when: Once a month, a week before the main buying or production decisions
When the review is a meeting, to get an agenda and a demand and supply gap list
When one worry dominates, to see three scenarios, their cost and a response for each
At the start of the review, to see how last month's forecast held up

tasks.task: Plan for a late shipment, a demand spike or a supplier failure

items.when: When you need the top risks ranked with a backup and an owner for each
When weighing one named worry, to compare three scenarios and what each costs
When the plan is drafted, to test several things going wrong at once
When one supplier or one route could stop the business and the record so far looks calm

tasks.task: Plan stock counts and explain a count variance

items.when: When counts are rare or rushed, to set a rolling schedule and who counts what
When the count differs from the system, to split timing, unit and counting errors
When variances repeat, to reconcile each count against its movements
When the counted stock must be valued, with write-downs flagged

tasks.task: Plan stock across warehouses and sales channels

items.when: When stock sits in more than one place, to set how much each should hold
When stock goes to Amazon, to plan how much to send and when, with a shipment checklist
When each location is planned, to check the totals still meet the service level

tasks.task: Tell customers and the team about shortages and dates

items.when: Before any date is given, to see what can really be delivered and when
When a product will be out of stock, to write a short update with the facts and next step
When delays are common, to set up an update flow and a delay script
When chasing a late supplier, to try a version they will want to help with
Before the update goes, to read it as the customer and list what they would still ask

always.when: Before any plan or forecast is shared, to find broken formulas and totals that do not add up
When a plan rests on a lead time, a service level or a growth rate, to log it and its risk

helpers.when: When suppliers must be found, tendered or renegotiated, not just ordered from
When freight booking, customs papers and warehouse receiving need running day to day
When product costs, overhead shares and stock value must tie to the accounts
When sales history is large or messy and needs proper cleaning and analysis first
When a quality failure needs a corrective action record or a supplier audit
When stock plans depend on Amazon limits, fees and inbound rules

gaps: No library item rebuilds demand hidden by stockouts before a forecast is made

No library item turns a production schedule and bills of materials into a dated materials buy list
No library item writes a purchase order pack with Incoterms rule, place and terms
No library item plans in-process quality checks for a small maker: what to check, when and the pass rule
No library item estimates demand for a new product from similar products' launch curves
No library item reports stock turns, days of cover and service level as a monthly planning scorecard
